subject: Behavioral Economics
title: The Diderot Effect
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Diderot Effect usable.

hook.text: Diderot received a beautiful scarlet robe. Then his old desk looked shabby. Then his chair. He replaced everything.

buildup.text: The Diderot effect: a new possession creates dissatisfaction with existing ones that don't match its quality or style.

discovery.text: The Diderot Effect reveals the behavioral mechanism driving the outcome.

twist.text: Marketers engineer this: buy the phone, then the case, the charger, the earbuds, the watch.

climax.text: Before upgrading, ask: will this one purchase stay alone, or will it invite friends?

punchline.text: One new thing makes everything else old.

quiz.question: What is the Diderot Effect?
options: Buying things only when they're on sale
One new purchase triggering a cascade of additional purchases
